abstract: Evaluates specimen integrity, coupon recovery protocols, and extraction depths
system_message:
You are the Metallurgical forensic specialist (METL), responsible for evaluating specimen integrity, coupon recovery protocols, extraction depths, and onshore lab capacity for subsea pipeline forensic investigations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Evaluates specimen integrity, coupon recovery protocols, and extraction depths（METSPEC）
information_points.content:
METL-METSPEC-I9X：For the Manned Saturation Habitat and Direct Metallurgical Coring Protocol, metallurgical coupon recovery protocol authorization is confirmed for the cut-out operation, with a maximum seabed excavation depth of 5.2 m required to expose the buried pipe underbelly.
METL-METSPEC-SQM：For the Cabled Crawling Crawler and High-Definition Photogrammetry Protocol, metallurgical coupon recovery protocol authorization is confirmed for the pipe cut-out operation, and the maximum seabed excavation depth is 3.6 m.
METL-METSPEC-021：For the Autonomous ROV Trenching and Ultrasonic Tomography Protocol, metallurgical coupon recovery protocol authorization is confirmed for the damaged pipeline segment cut-out operation, and the maximum seabed excavation depth is 3.6 m to clear sediment beneath the failure zone.

information_points.title: Onshore lab capacity（LABCAP）
information_points.content:
METL-LABCAP-42G：For the Autonomous ROV Trenching and Ultrasonic Tomography Protocol, the spectrometric assay lead time at the Aberdeen material analysis laboratory is 24 h.
METL-LABCAP-X7V：For the Cabled Crawling Crawler and High-Definition Photogrammetry Protocol, the spectrometric assay lead time at the Aberdeen material analysis laboratory is 48 h.
METL-LABCAP-3M4：For the Manned Saturation Habitat and Direct Metallurgical Coring Protocol, the spectrometric assay lead time at the Aberdeen material analysis laboratory is 72 h.
